newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Proton names new chief.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Proton names new chief.

text.p: The parent companies of Malaysian car maker Proton on Thursday named a new chairman to succeed the late Yahaya Ahmad, and assured investors that policies would not change.

Transportation and heavy industrial group DRB-Hicom said Saleh Sulong, 46, deputy chairman of the group and long-time partner of Yahaya, would take over as chairman effective immediately. Saleh had been widely expected to assume the post.
"I am most humbled and honoured by the confidence placed in me...," Saleh told a news conference. He said his appointment had been endorsed by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
It was Mahathir who, in 1995, picked Yahaya to revamp national carmaker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton).
"The vision, mission and strategies set down by...Yahaya will be continued," Saleh said. Major projects and programmes initiated "will be pursued with the same vigour, drive and pace".

Saleh, former deputy chairman of Proton, managing director of DRB and a director of Hicom, said he would absorb all responsibilities of Yahaya, who was killed in a helicopter crash on Monday night along with his wife and pilot.

Before his death, he was dubbed Malaysia's 'car tsar' and virtually controlled the nation's transport industry. He had stakes in various local automotive concerns as well as a controlling share in British sports car maker Group Lotus Ltd.
Shares in the seven companies in the DRB-Hicom group and two others controlled by Yahaya were suspended on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange on Tuesday after his death.

Saleh said the seven DRB-Hicom stocks -- Proton, Diversified Resources Bhd (DRB), Hicom Holdings Bhd, Edaran Otomobil Nasional, Kedah Cement Holdings Bhd, Gadek (Malaysia) Bhd and Gadek Capital Bhd -- will be requoted on Monday.
The suspension on Yahaya's two other companies -- Golden Pharos Bhd and Eastern Pacific Industrial Corp Bhd -- will be lifted the same day, he said.
Salleh said DRB-Hicom had also decided not make any other changes to its management.
